findings.title: Google API hub MCP reaches GA with OAuth scopes and Model Armor integration

visible_dates.basis: Google Cloud release notes section dated July 24, 2026.

findings.summary: Google Cloud made the API hub MCP server generally available. The release adds read/write AI-agent actions over API assets, global endpoint routing, service-specific OAuth scopes for read-only and read-write access, and Model Armor integration to protect MCP tool invocations from prompt injection and related attacks.
findings.evidence_classification: official product security control; MCP release note
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Google Cloud API hub MCP server GA; apihub.googleapis.com/mcp; apihub.readonly and apihub.readwrite OAuth scopes; Model Armor tool-invocation protection.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This turns MCP access to an API catalog into a managed cloud control point where least-privilege OAuth scopes and prompt-injection defenses can be applied before agents discover, modify, or deploy API assets.

upstream_routing.reason: Google Cloud, Apigee API hub, and Model Armor are broad AI/cloud ecosystem entities.
Granular OAuth scopes, MCP prompt-injection protection, and agent write-action controls are local security topics.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence because the source is an official Google Cloud release note with explicit security-relevant controls.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare this to local MCP authorization and final-action authorization leaves.
Route broad API hub and Model Armor product coverage upstream.

findings.title: Network-AI AgentRuntime sandbox path traversal permits out-of-sandbox file reads

visible_dates.basis: GitHub advisory date retained as older corroborating advisory, not as the in-window qualifying date.

findings.summary: SentinelOne published CVE-2026-58481 for Network-AI versions before 5.12.2. AgentRuntime used raw string prefix checks for sandbox path containment, so a base path such as /tmp/network-ai-sandbox could match sibling paths such as /tmp/network-ai-sandbox_evil, allowing agent users to read or list files outside the intended sandbox.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Network-AI multi-agent orchestrator versions before 5.12.2; AgentRuntime.readFile and AgentRuntime.listDir sandbox path containment.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent file tools rely on exact containment. Prefix-based checks break least privilege and can expose secrets or project data to an agent session that appears sandboxed.

upstream_routing.reason: Network-AI and Claude Code product/entity background route upstream.
Agent filesystem path containment and sandbox bypass implications are local security topics.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for technical details and fixed version from SentinelOne and the GitHub advisory. The in-window qualifying date is the SentinelOne publication date; the underlying CVE was older.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare to existing agent-tool filesystem path containment coverage.
Preserve the distinction between CVE publication date and in-window vulnerability-database publication date.

findings.title: Network-AI poisoned backup manifests can trigger recursive deletion

visible_dates.basis: GitHub advisory date retained as older corroborating advisory, not as the in-window qualifying date.

findings.summary: SentinelOne published CVE-2026-58484 for Network-AI versions before 5.12.2. EnvironmentManager.listBackups reads each backup manifest and trusts the manifest path field; pruneBackups then passes that path to recursive rmSync. A local actor able to write a backup manifest can cause arbitrary filesystem paths writable by the Network-AI process to be deleted.
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Network-AI and Network-AI Claude Code plugin versions before 5.12.2; EnvironmentManager backup prune behavior; data/<env>/.backups manifests.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent orchestration runtimes often persist environment snapshots and backups. Treating metadata as authority turns a local write primitive into destructive action under the agent runtime identity.

upstream_routing.reason: Network-AI and Claude Code product/entity background route upstream.
Agent runtime restore, backup, and destructive filesystem controls are local security topics.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for technical details and fixed version from SentinelOne and the GitHub advisory. The in-window qualifying date is the SentinelOne publication date; the underlying CVE was older.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare to infrastructure-and-supply-chain restore-path traversal coverage.
Record monitoring recommendations for backup manifest writes and prune executions if a local leaf is updated.

findings.title: Researchers report AI agent sandbox escape reaching host Mac files
findings.summary: Secure.com reported a chain in which researchers connected a single folder to a local AI agent session, then used a Linux kernel flaw identified as CVE-2026-46331 and design gaps to move from a Linux VM to host Mac file access. The report says SSH keys and cloud credentials were reachable, the product now defaults agent work to the cloud, and the local path does not appear to apply there.
findings.evidence_classification: security research report; sandbox escape; incident-style disclosure
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Local AI agent sandbox using a Linux VM with shared host mount; Linux kernels v5.18 through v7.1-rc6 for the referenced pedit COW primitive; host Mac file boundary.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent sandboxes often combine VM isolation, shared mounts, and host credential assumptions. A kernel primitive plus permissive host sharing can turn a narrow folder grant into broader host compromise.

upstream_routing.reason: General local-agent workspace and verification workflow lessons route upstream.
Sandbox escape, host credential exposure, shared-mount containment, and local-runtime mitigation are local security topics.

findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence. The article gives concrete technical details and visible dates, but ingest should corroborate CVE-2026-46331 and vendor status with primary CVE/vendor records before treating the chain as fully confirmed.
follow_up_actions: Find primary CVE or kernel maintainer references before updating durable pages.
Frame the local lesson around shared-mount and credential-boundary controls unless primary evidence supports broader claims.

findings.title: Darktrace expands email and collaboration controls for AI-agent-facing workflows

visible_dates.basis: Darktrace page includes a July 24, 2026 section for Darktrace / EMAIL capability expansion.

findings.summary: Darktrace described new Darktrace / EMAIL capabilities for email and collaboration workflows used by humans and AI agents. The updates include inbox analysis that highlights risky content, enhanced just-in-time training banners, custom sensitive-data detection for DLP workflows, and risk posture dashboards spanning Email, Microsoft Teams, Slack, and Zoom.
findings.evidence_classification: security control release; product security research and controls
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Darktrace / EMAIL; Adaptive Human Defense; email, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Zoom; custom sensitive-data detection; process-level workflow risk posture.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Email and collaboration systems increasingly hold prompts, approvals, credentials, and AI-agent instructions. Controls that detect sensitive-data flow and risky approval workflows help reduce prompt-injection, phishing, and delegated-authority risks around agent-facing communication channels.

upstream_routing.reason: Darktrace product background routes upstream if needed.
AI-agent communication-channel controls, DLP, phishing, and workflow-risk posture are local security topics.

findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence. The capabilities are concrete, but the page is product-positioned; ingest should keep it as control-release evidence rather than an independent incident or standard.
follow_up_actions: Use only the concrete control deltas if updating local pages.
